account: Today I have been keeping my appointments, though the ten o'clock grain inspection at the mill remained incomplete: I could not locate the miller or obtain grain quantities or storage records. I gave the secretary a written report and proposed tomorrow at ten for a follow-up, subject to checking appointments and obtaining the miller's confirmation. No findings about grain condition or supply are established. The secretary reports no council letters or urgent correspondence. An eighteen hundred great hall lighting inspection with the builder has been added to today's schedule; this appears to be ordinary town business. I also have fifteen hundred tea with my neighbour at a dockside cottage, followed by office time at sixteen thirty. The unusual matter is a repeated rumour of a bridge or port change associated with the bakery. Townsfolk named the baker, innkeeper and neighbour as having been there, but I have not witnessed such a discussion or received an actual proposal. I do not know what change is intended, who supports it, or its purpose. Repetition does not confirm it. The baker is now here near me and the secretary, but has not yet explained why. I should distinguish any firsthand account from the circulating rumour.
